scrollModel:
SCROLL → DISTANCE: a monotone piecewise map with dwells, not a linear one.

Measured facts (confirmed by running journey.js, do not re-derive): PATH_LENGTH = 162 tiles. Stops at d = 5, 22, 42, 68, 90, 116, 155 — gaps 5, 17, 20, 26, 22, 26, 39, tail 7. Every stop lands on a downward segment. The sea occupies d ∈ [122, 128).

The section's scroll is a table of ramps built at refresh:

  for each STOP:  travel-ramp (d_prev → stop.at), then dwell-ramp (d constant at stop.at)
  finally:        travel-ramp (155 → 162)

15 ramps total. `distanceAt(scrollPx)` binary-searches the table. A dwell ramp consumes scroll but no distance — the character stands still while the banner is readable, and the walk cycle freezes on its own because the frame index is a function of d. This is the single most important decision here: without dwells, a stop is a zero-width event and reading a card requires the user to hold the scroll perfectly still.

Constants (one block, all tunable):
  ZOOM        = clamp(2, round(viewH / (TILE*15)), 4)      integer, ~15 tiles tall on screen
  SPEED_R     = 1.6      screen px the map moves per px scrolled
  PX_PER_TILE = TILE*ZOOM / SPEED_R = 10*ZOOM
  DWELL_PX    = 0.40 * stageH
  EASE_PX     = 0.18 * stageH   (per travel ramp, split across its two ends)

Total section scroll = 162*10*ZOOM + 7*DWELL_PX + 8*EASE_PX. At ZOOM 3 / 900px viewport that is 4860 + 2520 + 1296 ≈ 8700px ≈ 9.6 viewport heights. State this as a decision, not an accident: the user asked for the whole page to behave like the walk. If it needs shortening, SPEED_R is the knob (2.2 → ~7 screens); do not shorten by cutting DWELL_PX, that is the readable part.

Ramp shape: linear in the middle, eased at both ends, so he decelerates into every stop and accelerates out. d = d0 + (d1-d0)*F(u) where F is the normalised integral of a trapezoid speed profile v(t) = smoothstep(t/k)*smoothstep((1-t)/k), k = clamp(0.06, EASE_PX/(2*rampPx), 0.5). Integrate v over ~24 fixed steps once per ramp at build time and cache the CDF; runtime is a lookup + lerp. A single smootherstep over a whole ramp is wrong — on the 39-tile stretch its peak speed is 1.875× average and he visibly sprints in the middle.

Wiring: ScrollTrigger.create({ trigger: stage, start:'top top', end: () => '+='+total, pin:true, anticipatePin:1, invalidateOnRefresh:true }). onUpdate stores `scrollPx = self.progress * total` and does nothing else; all work happens in a gsap.ticker callback, which is the same loop Lenis already drives (scroll.js line 30), so there is exactly one render per frame and no ordering hazard. No scrub — Lenis is already smoothing the input, and a second smoothing stage would make the character lag his own banner. Never window.scrollTo; any jump affordance (e.g. clicking a region rail) must go through lenis.scrollTo(px).
cameraModel:
The camera LEADS in the direction of travel — it does not centre and does not lag.

Vertical: the player is parked at 0.42 of stage height when walking down (so 58% of the view is the road ahead), 0.58 when walking up, 0.50 when moving sideways or standing. The anchor itself is damped (tau 0.35s, frame-rate corrected: `a += (target-a) * (1 - exp(-dt/tau))`) so the flip at a corner is a glide, not a snap. camY = clamp(0, footY*Z - stageH*leadY, mapH*Z - stageH). The distance→position mapping is direct, never damped — damping d would let the banner and the character disagree during fast scrolls.

Corner interaction (this is why the lead is damped rather than instant): five of the seven stops sit within 5 tiles of a PATH corner — barch 5 vs corner 8, chadda 22 between corners 18 and 26, jaiswal 68 vs 64, metarch2 116 vs 112, kfupm 155 vs 150. So the facing flips while a banner is on screen. Rule: while a banner is in state 'in', freeze leadY at its current value (stop re-targeting). A map-anchored card being yanked 8% of the viewport mid-read is the failure this prevents.

Horizontal: two regimes.
  mapW*Z <= stageW  → no horizontal camera at all. camX = -(stageW - mapW*Z)/2, i.e. the map is centred and never slides. The map is 34 tiles = 544px, so this is the ZOOM 2 case on any desktop ≥ 1100px.
  mapW*Z > stageW   → dead-zone follow. The player may move within ±0.18*stageW of centre before camX moves; outside that, camX damps toward the edge of the dead zone (tau 0.25s), clamped to [0, mapW*Z - stageW]. The path swings between col 6 and col 24, so without a dead zone every corner produces a full lateral pan and the section becomes unpleasant to look at.

Pixel integrity (non-negotiable for this art):
  - ZOOM is an integer and the canvas backing store uses an integer dpr (clamp to 1 or 2). Effective scale Z = ZOOM*dpr must be a whole number.
  - camX/camY are rounded to whole device pixels at draw time only, never in state, or the offsets ratchet.
  - ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false, and CSS `image-rendering: pixelated` on the canvas.
  With integer Z and integer offsets, each source texel occupies exactly Z aligned screen pixels and the tilemap stops crawling.

Rendering: build the map ONCE into offscreen canvases at 1× (544 × 1664 px, ~3.6 MB RGBA) — do not replay Scene.ops per frame. Two layers: `ground` (grass/beach/farm/water/path blobs) and `props` (houses, trees, decor). Per frame: blit the ground viewport rect, blit the props viewport rect, draw the player, then re-draw from a small pre-sorted list `tall[]` — props whose baseline is within ±3 tiles of the path — any whose baseline y is below the player's feet, so he passes behind them. That is a handful of extra drawImage calls and it closes the y-sort gap (HANDOFF §9.6 item 4) for the only place it is visible. Zoom changes cost nothing: the offscreen is always 1×, only the blit scale changes.
playerAnimation:
The walk frame is a PURE FUNCTION OF DISTANCE, not an accumulator and not wall-clock:

  frame = mod(floor(d / STRIDE), 6)      STRIDE = 0.25 tiles per frame

That single line answers all three failure modes at once. It cannot drift (no accumulation), it reverses correctly when the user scrolls up (floor of a decreasing d walks the frames backwards, so the legs run in reverse — which is right), and it freezes automatically inside a dwell because d is constant there. No moonwalk is possible, because there is no time term.

STRIDE = 0.25 gives 1.5 tiles per 6-frame cycle — about right for a 32px character on 16px tiles. In scroll terms one animation frame per 2.5*ZOOM px of scroll; a 100px wheel notch, smoothed by Lenis over ~1.15s, plays roughly 13 frames ≈ 11fps, a natural walk rate. Clamp the frame advance to 2 per rAF so a fling does not strobe the legs.

Row selection (player.webp, 6 cols × 10 rows of 32×32):
  moving:  down → row 3, up → row 5, left/right → row 4
  still:   down → row 0, up → row 2, left/right → row 1
  The side rows are one facing only; flip with ctx.scale(-1,1) for the other. Confirm which way the sheet faces in /lab/tiles.html rather than guessing — assume it faces right until checked.

Direction: do NOT read pointAt(d).dir directly. It flips exactly at a vertex, and when d sits on one it jitters. Sample a chord instead — dir = axis(pointAt(d+0.4) - pointAt(d-0.4)) — which smooths the turn over 0.8 tiles. If d is decreasing (scrolling up), invert the direction so he faces the way he is actually going.

Idle: `still` is true when ramp.kind === 'dwell' or |Δd| < 0.004 tiles. Idle is the one animation allowed to be time-driven — frame = floor(time/160) % 6 — because a standing breath is not locomotion and cannot moonwalk. While standing at a stop he turns to face the building: dir = stop.side < 0 ? 'left' : 'right', idle-side row 1, flipped per side. He arrives, stops, turns to the door, and the card is up. That reads as arrival.

Also draw a flat dark ellipse shadow under his feet, offset a pixel bottom-right, per the craft rules in §9 — without it he floats over the road. Anchor: feet at map px (p.x*16 + 8, p.y*16 + 16); draw the 32×32 frame at (feetX-16, feetY-32).
bannerLifecycle:
A state machine with hysteresis, not a scrubbed opacity. Scrubbing opacity to |d - stop.at| looks mushy and flickers when the user parks the scroll on a boundary; a state machine plus a CSS transition gives the card its own timing.

Thresholds, in path-distance tiles:
  ENTER_R = 4.5   mount when |d - stop.at| < 4.5
  EXIT_R  = 6.0   unmount only when |d - stop.at| > 6.0
  hysteresis band = 1.5 tiles

Safe because the smallest gap between stops is 17 tiles (barch→chadda): two windows can never overlap, so at most one banner exists at any time. Assert this at build time — if STOPS ever move closer than 2*EXIT_R = 12 tiles, the invariant breaks.

Lifecycle:
  approach → at d = at-4.5 the element is created, appended, and gets `.is-in` on the next rAF: 180ms fade + 8px rise.
  hold     → the card is at full opacity across the approach, the entire DWELL_PX of scroll, and the departure. The hold is measured in scroll pixels (DWELL_PX ≈ 0.40*viewH), not in distance, which is what makes it readable at any scroll speed.
  clear    → past d = at+6.0, `.is-in` is removed (220ms fade-out) and the node is removed on transitionend.
  MIN_SHOW_MS = 450 — a card that has just mounted cannot fade out before 450ms have elapsed, so a fast scroll still shows it.
  If a new stop wants to mount while the old one is inside MIN_SHOW, the old node is removed immediately with no fade. Never queue; never let two cards crossfade.

Special case, the last stop: kfupm's exit at 155+6 = 161 falls one tile before PATH_LENGTH = 162, so under the uniform rule the card blinks out just before the section unpins. Suppress the exit for the final stop — hold it while d > 155 until the section unpins. It is the present day; ending on it lands better than ending on empty road.

Placement: anchored to the building, not a fixed HUD — "wherever it is crossing that banner is coming" means the card belongs to the place. transform = translate3d(stopAnchor(stop).col*TILE*Z - camX ± offset, row*TILE*Z - camY, 0), positioned absolutely inside the pinned stage so it pins with it, side chosen from stop.side (card on the same side as the building), clamped 12px inside the stage on both axes. Below 900px stage width, switch to a fixed bottom sheet instead — there is no room beside a 6-tile building at that width.

Content: build the card from the existing `<ol class="timeline">` li matching `[data-stop="<id>"]`, NOT from the STOPS strings. That keeps one copy of the text, keeps it crawlable, and makes i18n free (§9.6 item 7 disappears). Re-read the current card on the `sa:languagechange` event, the way skills.js does with its tooltip.

Accessibility: the map canvas is aria-hidden. Keep the `<ol>` in the DOM under a visually-hidden class rather than `[hidden]` — skills.js uses `list.hidden = true`, which drops it from the a11y tree; here the list is the only copy of the content, so it must stay readable by screen readers.
edgeCases: SCROLLING BACKWARDS — d decreases; the frame formula mod(floor(d/STRIDE),6) runs the walk cycle in reverse on its own, and the chord-sampled direction is inverted so he faces up/left instead of down/right. Banners re-mount symmetrically on the way back up, and the dwells still cost scroll going up, so the reverse walk pauses at each stop too. Nothing special to write except the direction inversion.

FAST SCROLL PAST A STOP — three guards. (1) The dwell ramp means a stop cannot be crossed without consuming DWELL_PX of scroll, so it is never zero-width. (2) MIN_SHOW_MS = 450 keeps a mounted card up even if d has already left its window. (3) A fling guard: if |Δd| in one frame exceeds 10 tiles, mount nothing and clear any current card without a fade — flinging from the top of the page to the bottom must not strobe seven cards. When velocity drops back under the threshold, whatever stop is in window mounts normally.

THE SEA CROSSING — d ∈ [122, 128), exactly 6 tiles at col 24, rows 70-75, and it is the one stretch with no ground under him. Draw bridge.webp over those path cells: the asset exists, and §9.9 rule 5 says regions are separated by something you cross, which is precisely what the India→Saudi transition should be. The walk needs no special case on a bridge. Note the tight coincidence: metarch2 (at 116) clears at 116+6.0 = 122.0, the exact shoreline — the card releases as he steps onto the bridge. That is good timing but it is exact; if EXIT_R is ever raised the card will hang over the water.

REDUCED MOTION — return before anything is built, exactly as skills.js does at line 114. No pin, no canvas, no offscreen render, no sheet loading. The existing <ol class="timeline"> stays visible and is the section. Do not substitute a static map image; a 9-screen pinned section replaced by a decorative picture is worse than the list.

NARROW VIEWPORTS — below 640px of stage width, fall back to the timeline list (same rule and same MIN_W as the skills field). At ZOOM 3 a 390px phone shows 8 tiles across; a house is 6 tiles wide and the camera would pan constantly. Between 640 and 900px, force ZOOM 2 and switch banners to the fixed bottom sheet. Re-evaluate on a debounced resize and rebuild rather than leaving a half-pinned section, and call ScrollTrigger.refresh() (projects.js line 71 is the precedent).

CORNERS UNDER A BANNER — five stops are within 5 tiles of a PATH corner, so the camera lead flips while a card is anchored to a building. Freeze leadY while a banner is in state 'in'. Without this the card slides several percent of the viewport mid-read.

REFRESH / RESIZE / FONT LOAD / LANGUAGE SWITCH — the ramp table depends on stageH and ZOOM, so rebuild it in onRefreshInit and use invalidateOnRefresh + end:()=>'+='+total. ScrollTrigger preserves progress across a refresh, so d is preserved too. The offscreen map never needs re-rendering — it is always 1×. main.js already refreshes on fonts.ready, load, and language change.

OFF-SCREEN AND HIDDEN TAB — run the ticker callback only while the trigger is active (onToggle) and pause on visibilitychange, as skills.js does. The per-frame cost is two blits plus a sprite, but a pinned 9-screen section should not burn a frame budget when it is nowhere near the viewport.

PRE-EXISTING BUG TO FIX FIRST, NOT PART OF THIS TASK — stopAnchor(barch) returns col = round(6 + (-1*6)) - 3 = -3. lab/journey.html clamps it to 0, so BIT Mesra is jammed against the left edge of the map, half off. barch sits at x = 6 with side = -1 and there is simply not 6 tiles of room to its left. Either move the first PATH corner right or flip barch's side; whichever, the camera will frame an off-map building at d = 5 otherwise.
